title: EDC exposure during SC-islet differentiation
projectDescription: We aimed to asses how EDC exposure in combination with a genetic predisposition for diabetes could impact pancreatic endocrine cell development. For this, we used a protocol to generate Stem-cell islets (SC-islets) from induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) following a 7 satege protocol. For 2 weeks after pancreatic endocrine progenitor stage, cells were treated with a EDC mix of 1 nm of Bisphenol A, bisphenol S, and trans-nonachlor, or the vehicle DMSO. After those 2 weeks, the cells got a 1 week recovery period before collection. In the present study we used both iPSCs carrying the P291fsinC mutation in the HNF1A gene, and and isogenic non carrier control.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Cells were harvested, centrifuged at 300 g for 4 min and resuspended in 80 uL 8M Urea 200 mM EPPS pH8.5, protease inhibitor with EDTA. The samples were sonicated 3 times 30 seconds to lyse the cells. The samples were centrifuged at 14000 g for 3 min, and supernantant was collected. Protein concentration was determined using the BCA assay, and 100 ug of protein from each sample were processed. 25 mM Tris, 0.5 mM CasCl2 were added to each sample and slowly mixed for 5 min. 9 mM dithiothreitol were added to each sample and incubated for 1 hour. Afterwards, 20 mM iodoacetamide were added and incubated for 1 hour in dark. To quench the reaction, 1.6 mM dithiothreitol were added and incubated for 10 min. Before trypsination, 35 M Tris 0.7 M CaCl were added, and 2 ug of trypsin and left at 37 degrees over night on shaker. To stop the reaction, 0.8 % Formic acid were added. All peptides were desalted by Oasis plate, C18 column (Waters).   The TMT-labelling and fractionation protocol was performed as previously described (Liu et al. 2023). 25 ug of peptides from each sample were used for subsequent processing and dissolved in 40 uL of TEAB. 500 ug of TMTpro 16 plex reagents were dissolved in 75 uL acetonitrile. 12 uL of TMTpro 16 plex reagent is added to the samples of one 16 plex, incubated for 1 hour. The reaction was quenched by adding hydroxylamine to a final concentration of 0.3 %. All the TMT labeled samples across 1 plex was pooled before desalting using Oasis plate. The samples were frozen at negative 80 degrees before vacuum centrifugation to near dryness.   The TMT labeled samples was first fractioned using a Strong anion exchange spin column (Fisher Scientific, 10311514) by using 20 mM NH4OH and 15 % acetonitrile in combination with 0, 20, 50, 100, 250 and 500 mM ammonium acetate, creating 6 fractions. Fractions 0, 20 and 500 ammonium acetate were pooled, as well as fractions 100, 250 and 500 mM were a second pool. Each pool was frozen at -80 before vacuum centrifuged to near dryness. Each pool was desalted using StageTip (Fisher Scientific, 87784). Each fraction pool was subsequently fractionated using high pH reversed-Phase peptide fractionation (Fisher Scientific, 15362617). The fractions were collected by adding 0.1 % triethylamine with 7.5, 10, 12.5, 15, 17.5, 20, 22.5, 27.5, 30, 35 and 60% acetonitrile. The following fractions were pooled: 7.5 and 22.5, 10 and 25, 12,5 and 27,5, 15 and 30, 17.5 and 35, 20 and 60 % acetonitrile 0.1% triethylamine. Giving a total of 6 fractions per sax fraction, leading to a total of 12 fractions per 16-plex. Each fraction were frozen and vacuum dried to near dryness, before desalting with Stage tip.   From each of 12 non-adjacent fractions, ∼5 μg was dissolved in 5% aqueous formic acid (FA) /5% acetonitrile prior to LC-MS/MS analysis on an Orbitrap Eclipse mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific, San Jose, CA) coupled to a Neo Vanquish liquid chromatography (LC) pump (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Peptides were fractionated on a 100-μm inner diameter microcapillary column packed with ∼35 cm of Accucore resin (2.6 μm, 150 Å, ThermoFisher Scientific). For each analysis, we loaded ~1 μg onto the column.   The scan sequence began with an MS1 spectrum (Orbitrap analysis, resolution 60,000, 350-1350 Th, automatic gain control (AGC) target 4 x105, maximum injection time 50 ms). The hrMS2 stage consisted of fragmentation by higher energy collisional dissociation (HCD, normalized collision energy 36%) and analysis using the Orbitrap (AGC 200%, maximum injection time 86 ms, isolation window 0.6 Th, resolution 50,000). Data were acquired using the FAIMSpro interface the dispersion voltage (DV) set to 5,000V, the compensation voltages (CVs) were set at -40V, -60V, and -80V, and the TopSpeed parameter was set at 1 sec per CV.
dataProcessingProtocol: Mass spectra were processed using a Comet-based in-house software pipeline (Huttlin, Jedrychowski et al. 2010), and spectra were converted to mzXML using a modified version of ReAdW.exe. Database searching included all entries from the human Uniprot database (March, 2021). This database was concatenated with one composed of all protein sequences in the reversed order. Searches were performed using a 50 ppm precursor ion tolerance for total protein level analysis. The product ion tolerance was set to 0.9 Da. These wide mass tolerance windows were chosen to maximize sensitivity in conjunction with Sequest searches and linear discriminant analysis (Beausoleil, Villen et al. 2006, Huttlin, Jedrychowski et al. 2010). TMTpro tags on lysine residues and peptide N termini (+304.207) and carbamidomethylation of cysteine residues (+57.021 Da) were set as static modifications, while oxidation of methionine residues (+15.995 Da) was set as a variable modification. Peptide-spectrum matches (PSMs) were adjusted to a 1% false discovery rate (FDR) (Elias and Gygi 2007, Elias and Gygi 2010). PSM filtering was performed using a linear discriminant analysis, as described previously (Huttlin, Jedrychowski et al. 2010), while considering the following parameters: XCorr, ΔCn, missed cleavages, peptide length, charge state, and precursor mass accuracy. For TMT-based reporter ion quantitation, we extracted the summed signal-to-noise (S/N) ratio for each TMT channel and found the closest matching centroid to the expected mass of the TMT reporter ion.  The search space for each reporter ion was limited to a range of 0.003 m/z to prevent overlap between the isobaric reporter ions. For protein-level comparisons, PSMs were identified, quantified, and collapsed to a 1% peptide false discovery rate (FDR) and then collapsed further to a final protein-level FDR of 1%. Moreover, protein assembly was guided by principles of parsimony to produce the smallest set of proteins necessary to account for all observed peptides.  Proteins were quantified by summing reporter ion counts across all matching PSMs using in-house software, as described previously (Huttlin, Jedrychowski et al. 2010). PSMs with poor quality, MS3 spectra with TMT reporter summed signal-to-noise ratio that is less than 100, or no MS3 spectra were excluded from quantitation (McAlister, Huttlin et al. 2012). Protein quantitation values were exported for further analysis in Microsoft Excel and GraphPad Prism (version 8). Each reporter ion channel was summed across all quantified proteins and normalized assuming equal protein loading of all samples.
